name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MCQ_Q01 - Preparation and reactions of alcohols and phenols

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding alcohols and phenols:

Statement I: Reaction of methanal with a Grignard reagent followed by hydrolysis yields a primary alcohol, whereas ketones under the same conditions yield tertiary alcohols.

Statement II: In the Lucas test using concentrated \(\mathrm{HCl}\) and anhydrous \(\mathrm{ZnCl_2}\), tertiary alcohols produce turbidity immediately at room temperature, whereas primary alcohols do not produce turbidity at room temperature.

Statement III: Treating phenol with bromine water produces a mixture of o-bromophenol and p-bromophenol as the major products, whereas treating phenol with \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) in \(\mathrm{CS_2}\) at \(273\text{ K}\) yields 2,4,6-tribromophenol as a white precipitate.

Statement IV: Acid-catalysed dehydration of alcohols follows the ease order tertiary > secondary > primary because the rate-determining step involves formation of a carbocation intermediate.

Which of the following is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nucleophilic addition of Grignard reagents to carbonyl compounds depends on the substituents attached to the carbonyl carbon. Reactivity of alcohols in \(\mathrm{C-O}\) bond cleavage reactions (Lucas test and acid-catalysed dehydration) is governed by carbocation stability, while electrophilic bromination of phenol depends on the polarity of the solvent medium.

Step 2: Evaluation of Grignard Reagent Addition
Methanal (\(\mathrm{HCHO}\)) has two hydrogen atoms attached to the carbonyl carbon; nucleophilic addition of \(\mathrm{RMgX}\) followed by hydrolysis forms \(\mathrm{RCH_2OH}\), a primary alcohol. Ketones (\(\mathrm{RCOR'}\)) have two alkyl groups attached to the carbonyl carbon, so addition of \(\mathrm{R''MgX}\) followed by hydrolysis produces a tertiary alcohol, \(\mathrm{RR'R''COH}\). Thus, the claim regarding Grignard reactions with methanal and ketones is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Lucas Test
Alcohols are soluble in Lucas reagent (concentrated \(\mathrm{HCl}\) and anhydrous \(\mathrm{ZnCl_2}\)), whereas the alkyl chlorides formed upon reaction are immiscible and cause turbidity. Tertiary alcohols form stable tertiary carbocations rapidly and therefore produce turbidity immediately at room temperature, whereas primary alcohols do not react appreciably at room temperature and show no turbidity. Thus, the claim regarding the Lucas test is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Bromination of Phenol
In a low-polarity solvent such as \(\mathrm{CS_2}\) at \(273\text{ K}\), phenol reacts with \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) to undergo monobromination, yielding o-bromophenol (minor) and p-bromophenol (major). In contrast, in aqueous medium (bromine water), phenol is ionised to the even more strongly activating phenoxide ion and undergoes rapid trisubstitution to give 2,4,6-tribromophenol as a white precipitate. Because the two reagent conditions and their products are interchanged, the claim regarding bromination of phenol is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of Acid-Catalysed Dehydration
In the mechanism of acid-catalysed dehydration, the protonated alcohol loses a water molecule in the slow, rate-determining step to form a carbocation. Since carbocation stability follows the order tertiary > secondary > primary, the relative ease of dehydration of alcohols also follows tertiary > secondary > primary. Thus, the claim regarding dehydration order and its mechanism is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding Grignard addition to methanal and ketones, the Lucas test behaviour of tertiary versus primary alcohols, and the carbocation-controlled dehydration order are correct, whereas the claim swapping the products of phenol bromination in bromine water and \(\mathrm{CS_2}\) is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III, and Statement IV are all correct.
Statement I, Statement II, and Statement IV are correct, while Statement III is incorrect.
Statement I, Statement III, and Statement IV are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.
Statement II and Statement III are correct, while Statement I and Statement IV are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MCQ_Q02 - Reactions of phenols and Williamson synthesis of aryl ethers

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding phenols and ethers:

Statement I: When phenol is treated with dilute nitric acid at \(298\text{ K}\), o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol are formed, and o-nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding whereas p-nitrophenol is less volatile due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

Statement II: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, treating phenol with chloroform in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide followed by acidification introduces a \(-\mathrm{CHO}\) group at the ortho position to form salicylaldehyde.

Statement III: In Kolbe's reaction, sodium phenoxide undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with carbon dioxide followed by acidification to yield 4-hydroxybenzoic acid as the main product.

Statement IV: In the preparation of 1-methoxy-4-nitrobenzene via Williamson synthesis, reacting 1-bromo-4-nitrobenzene with sodium methoxide is preferred over reacting sodium 4-nitrophenoxide with bromomethane.

Which of the following is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Electrophilic substitution in phenol and phenoxide ions is strongly directed towards the ortho and para positions. Physical separation of isomers depends on intramolecular versus intermolecular hydrogen bonding, while Williamson ether synthesis requires an unhindered alkyl halide for \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) displacement.

Step 2: Evaluation of Nitration and Steam Volatility
Nitration of phenol with dilute \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) at \(298\text{ K}\) produces a mixture of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol. In o-nitrophenol, intramolecular hydrogen bonding occurs within the same molecule, preventing molecular association and making it steam volatile. In p-nitrophenol, intermolecular hydrogen bonding causes association of molecules, lowering its volatility. Thus, the claim regarding nitration and steam volatility of nitrophenols is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reimer-Tiemann Reaction
Treating phenol with chloroform (\(\mathrm{CHCl_3}\)) and aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) forms an ortho-substituted benzal chloride intermediate, which upon alkaline hydrolysis and subsequent acidification (\(\mathrm{H^+}\)) yields salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde). Thus, the claim regarding the Reimer-Tiemann reaction is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Kolbe's Reaction
In Kolbe's reaction, sodium phenoxide reacts with the weak electrophile \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) followed by acidification to give 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid, commonly called salicylic acid) as the main product, not 4-hydroxybenzoic acid. Thus, the claim regarding Kolbe's reaction is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of Williamson Synthesis of 1-Methoxy-4-nitrobenzene
Williamson synthesis proceeds by an \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) mechanism in which an alkoxide or aryloxide attacks an alkyl halide. Reacting sodium 4-nitrophenoxide with bromomethane (\(\mathrm{CH_3Br}\)) readily gives 1-methoxy-4-nitrobenzene via \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) attack at the methyl carbon. In contrast, 1-bromo-4-nitrobenzene is an aryl halide whose \(\mathrm{C-Br}\) bond has partial double bond character and resists \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) displacement by methoxide under standard Williamson conditions. Thus, the claim preferring 1-bromo-4-nitrobenzene with sodium methoxide is incorrect.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding the nitration and steam volatility of o- and p-nitrophenols and the formation of salicylaldehyde in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction are correct, whereas the claims that Kolbe's reaction forms 4-hydroxybenzoic acid as the main product and that 1-bromo-4-nitrobenzene with sodium methoxide is preferred for preparing 1-methoxy-4-nitrobenzene are incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, and Statement III are correct, while Statement IV is incorrect.
Statement I and Statement IV are correct, while Statement II and Statement III are incorrect.
Statement II, Statement III, and Statement IV are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.
Statement I and Statement II are correct, while Statement III and Statement IV are incorrect.
